entry.title: Re: Safer sighashes and more granular SIGHASH_NOINPUT
entry.summary:
A transaction can be rebroadcast as a replacement for a mutated transaction under specific conditions related to the fee rate. If a new transaction is created with a fee rate that is at least the incremental relay fee below the original transaction's fee rate, this enables the original transaction to be considered for rebroadcast as a Replace-by-Fee (RBF) replacement. However, this process may not proceed if the mutated transaction has been pinned, which restricts its replacement.
The incremental relay fee is a parameter in Bitcoin’s configuration, set using -incrementalrelayfee=<amt>. This fee rate, measured in BTC per kilobyte, determines the cost threshold for relaying transactions within nodes’ memory pools. It plays a crucial role in limiting mempool growth and governs the rules for transaction replacement as defined by BIP 125. The default value for this parameter is 0.00001 BTC/kB.
Further information on the incremental relay fee can be found at [Bitcoin Core Documentation](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/master/doc/release-notes/release-notes-0.13.0.md#transaction-relay-and-fees).
